# Output Formats

The review writes two files. The YAML is the machine-readable state the optimize skill consumes. The markdown is the human report.

## `.intercom/content-review.yaml`

```yaml
# Content Review — generated by intercom-setup-review-content
reviewed_at: 2026-09-30
workspace_id: it7gods8
total_articles: 24          # returned by list_articles, including samples
reviewed: 23
excluded_samples: 1
scope_file: .intercom/scope.md   # or null if no scope defined

summary:
  ready: 6        # all 14 factors pass or n/a, no high help-center findings
  needs_work: 11  # no factor scored fail; one or more partial
  not_ready: 6    # at least one factor scored fail
  conflicts: 2
  duplicates: 1

articles:
  - id: "17234720"
    title: "Rate limits and 429 errors"
    state: draft
    updated_at: 2026-09-29
    parent: null
    in_scope: true            # true / false / unknown (no scope file)
    readiness: not_ready      # ready | needs_work | not_ready
    priority: 1               # 1 = optimize first
    factors:
      jobs_to_be_done:      { score: fail,    evidence: "Opens with a definition, no statement of what the reader will do" }
      disambiguation:       { score: pass }
      self_contained:       { score: partial, evidence: "'What to do' section doesn't name rate limits" }
      chunk_boundaries:     { score: partial, evidence: "Keyless limits and paid limits share one section" }
      query_answer_symmetry:{ score: partial, evidence: "Heading 'What to do' is not a customer question" }
      structured_enumeration: { score: fail,  evidence: "Backoff steps (1s, 2s, 4s) written inline, not numbered" }
      instruction_completeness: { score: partial, evidence: "No confirmation of what success looks like after retry" }
      numerical_clarity:    { score: fail,    evidence: "'Higher limits' and 'a maximum number of requests' — no values" }
      defined_terms:        { score: fail,    evidence: "'concurrency', '429' never defined" }
      audience:             { score: fail,    evidence: "No plan named; limits differ by plan" }
      limitations:          { score: pass }
      entity_distribution:  { score: partial, evidence: "'the limit' used without naming rate limit in section 2" }
      tables_context:       { score: n/a }
      visuals:              { score: n/a }
    help_center:
      - { check: description_length, severity: low, evidence: "Description OK (39 chars)" }
      - { check: draft_state, severity: info, evidence: "Draft — Fin won't use it until published" }
    conflicts: []
    notes: ""

conflicts:
  - subject: "Credit rollover on Enterprise plans"
    statements:
      - source: "article:17234725"
        text: "Enterprise plans roll credits over by a custom amount"
      - source: "https://docs.example.com/billing"
        text: "Annual Enterprise plans roll unused credits over 2 months"
    newer_source: "https://docs.example.com/billing"   # or unknown
    resolution: null   # filled in by the user, read by optimize

duplicates:
  - articles: ["17234712", "17234790"]
    shared_question: "How much does a scrape cost?"

coverage_gaps:            # omit if no conversations were sampled
  sampled_conversations: 120
  gaps:
    - topic: "Why was I charged for a 404 page?"
      conversations: 14
      matching_article: null
```

**Priority rule:** sort by (in_scope first) → readiness (`not_ready` before `needs_work`) → number of `fail` factors → number of `partial` factors → conversation volume if known. Priority `1` is optimized first.

**Readiness rule:**
- `ready` — every factor `pass` or `n/a`, and no `high` help-center finding
- `needs_work` — no factor `fail`, at least one `partial` or a `medium` help-center finding
- `not_ready` — at least one factor `fail`, or any `high` finding (including an unresolved conflict)

## `.intercom/reviews/YYYY-MM-DD.md`

```markdown
# Content Review — YYYY-MM-DD

**Workspace:** <id> · **Articles reviewed:** 23 (1 sample excluded) · **Scope:** <first job from scope.md, or "none defined">

## Summary

| Readiness | Articles |
|-----------|----------|
| Ready | 6 |
| Needs work | 11 |
| Not ready | 6 |

- **Source conflicts:** 2 (must be resolved before optimizing the affected articles)
- **Duplicates:** 1 pair
- **Most common failing factors:** numerical clarity (9), defined terms (8), audience (7)

## Conflicts to Resolve

For each conflict: subject, both statements with sources, which looks newer. Ask the user which is correct.

## Articles by Priority

| # | Article | State | Readiness | Fails | Partials | Top issue |
|---|---------|-------|-----------|-------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Rate limits and 429 errors | draft | Not ready | 5 | 4 | No plan-specific numbers |

## Factor Heatmap

Rows = articles, columns = factors 1–14, cells = ✓ / ~ / ✗ / –.
Introduce the table with one sentence explaining the symbols.

## Help Center Findings

Titles, descriptions, staleness, orphans, collection structure.

## Coverage Gaps

Only if conversations were sampled.

## Next Step

"Run **intercom-setup-optimize-content** to rewrite the priority articles."
```

Keep the report observational: state what is true of each article. Do not write replacement text here — that is the optimize skill's job.
